stem: I run beneath the piriformis, sometimes right through it too. Widest, longest nerve in you — split me at the knee, and you'll see. What am I?
The femoral triangle is bordered above by the inguinal ligament and laterally by sartorius. What forms its medial border?
A newborn's arm hangs limp after a difficult shoulder dystocia delivery, forearm pronated in the classic "waiter's tip" posture. Which nerve roots were stretched?
explanation: This is Erb's palsy (upper trunk, C5–C6).

stem: Fill in the blank: the ____ canal carries the femoral artery and vein (but not the nerve) from the femoral triangle into the popliteal fossa.
Nicknamed the "guardian bone" for shielding the brachial plexus and subclavian vessels as they cross beneath it. What bone is this?
I'm a triangle on the back of your hand, bounded by two thumb tendons — tap me and a tender scaphoid might be to blame. What am I?
A patient can't abduct the arm past 15° and the deltoid is wasted after a surgical neck of humerus fracture. Which nerve was injured?
Cantlie's line divides this organ into functional right and left lobes, independent of its visible surface fissures. Which organ?
A patient's ring and little fingers are permanently flexed at the DIP and PIP joints, unable to extend, after a wrist laceration. Which nerve was injured?
explanation: The 'ulnar paradox': distal ulnar lesions spare FDP to the ring and little fingers, so clawing is worse than with proximal lesions.

stem: Hesselbach's triangle — the site of direct inguinal hernias — is bordered by the rectus abdominis medially and the inguinal ligament inferiorly. What forms its third (lateral) border?
A patient can't dorsiflex the foot and has a "slapping" gait after a fibular neck fracture. Which nerve was compressed?
I'm a point one-third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus — press me in appendicitis and you'll wince. What am I?
Fill in the blank: ____ canal, on the medial wrist, transmits the ulnar nerve and artery into the hand.
Nicknamed the knee's "seatbelt" for preventing the tibia from sliding forward under the femur — which ligament is this?
A patient can't wrinkle the forehead or close one eye fully, with drooping on that entire side of the face. Which finding distinguishes this from a stroke?
choices: Sparing of the mouth only occurs in stroke
Both eyes are always affected in stroke
There is no reliable distinguishing sign
explanation: This pattern is typical of Bell's palsy; upper motor neuron lesions such as stroke spare the forehead.

stem: Horner's syndrome classically presents with ptosis, miosis, and ____.
choices: Ptosis of the lower lid only

stem: Fill in the blank: the three cords of the brachial plexus are named for their relation to the axillary artery — lateral, medial, and ____.
I pierce the diaphragm at three separate levels — T8 for the vena cava, T10 for the esophagus, and T12 for the aorta. What am I describing?
Which rotator cuff muscle initiates the first 15° of shoulder abduction before the deltoid takes over?
A patient has numbness in the thumb, index, and middle fingers along with weak thumb opposition, worse at night. Which nerve is compressed, and where?
choices: Median nerve at the carpal tunnel
Radial nerve at the spiral groove
Ulnar nerve at the cubital tunnel

stem: I widen when you inhale and narrow when you exhale — a heart sound gap that shifts with the breathing cycle. What splits me?
A diver breath-holds and their oxygen saturation stays near-normal for nearly a minute before suddenly plunging as PaO2 falls further. Which curve explains this delayed, then steep, drop?
The renal handling triad includes glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption, and ____ — active or passive movement of substances from peritubular capillaries into the tubule lumen.
A patient's blood pressure drops on standing with no compensatory rise in heart rate. Failure of which reflex arc explains this?
Fill in the blank: the ____ effect describes how rising CO2 lowers hemoglobin's oxygen affinity, aiding oxygen unloading in active tissue.
Think of me as the heart's built-in "overdraft protection" — I let it pump out whatever volume flows in, matching output to venous return. What law am I?
An ECG shows progressively lengthening PR intervals until a QRS is dropped, then the pattern repeats. What conduction abnormality is this?
explanation: Mobitz type I is also called Wenckebach.

stem: The Fick principle for measuring cardiac output uses oxygen consumption, arterial oxygen content, and ____.
I'm released from the posterior pituitary, but actually made in the hypothalamus — I clamp down your kidneys' water channels when you're dehydrated. What am I?
explanation: ADH is also called vasopressin.

stem: A diver who ascends too quickly develops joint pain and neurologic symptoms as gas comes out of solution in blood and tissue. Which gas law explains why gas dissolved at depth in the first place?
Fill in the blank: net fluid movement across capillary walls depends on hydrostatic pressure and ____ pressure (the Starling forces).
Cushing's reflex, triggered by rising intracranial pressure, classically shows hypertension, irregular respirations, and ____.
Which phase of the cardiac cycle occurs immediately after the mitral valve closes but before the aortic valve opens, when ventricular volume doesn't change?
Fill in the blank: the Henderson–Hasselbalch equation relates pH to the ratio of bicarbonate to dissolved ____.
Constriction of which renal arteriole increases glomerular filtration rate by raising pressure within the glomerulus?
Oxygen delivery to tissue depends on cardiac output multiplied by ____.
I explain why a dilated, thin-walled ventricle needs more wall tension to generate the same pressure as a smaller one — increasing myocardial oxygen demand. What law am I?
Central chemoreceptors in the medulla primarily respond to changes in which gas, while peripheral chemoreceptors respond most strongly to falling levels of the other?
Fill in the blank: a mid-cycle surge of ____ triggers ovulation roughly 36 hours later.
A patient hyperventilates during a panic attack and develops perioral tingling and carpal spasm. What is the primary mechanism?
Three enzymes gate the slowest steps of glycolysis: hexokinase, PFK-1, and pyruvate kinase. What do these three have in common?
choices: They are all rate-limiting enzymes of glycolysis
They are all found only in the liver
They are all inhibited by insulin

stem: A child has coarse facial features, corneal clouding, and hepatosplenomegaly, with excess dermatan and heparan sulfate in the urine. Which enzyme is deficient?
explanation: Alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency causes Hurler syndrome.

stem: The urea cycle's mitochondrial and cytosolic intermediates include carbamoyl phosphate, citrulline, and ____ before ornithine regenerates the cycle.
A patient with chronic alcohol use develops confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia. This classic triad points to deficiency of which vitamin?
explanation: Confusion, ataxia and ophthalmoplegia form Wernicke's triad.

stem: Think of me as a rechargeable battery your cells swap for work, not long-term storage. What molecule am I?
Fill in the blank: ____ deficiency causes phenylalanine to build up, leading to intellectual disability if untreated — screened for at birth.
explanation: Phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency is phenylketonuria (PKU).

stem: An older patient's urine darkens to black on standing, with dark cartilage staining and arthritis. Which enzyme is deficient?
explanation: Homogentisate oxidase deficiency causes alkaptonuria.

stem: The relationship between enzyme reaction rate and substrate concentration, producing a hyperbolic curve, is described by which equation?
I'm the cell's "recycling truck" — I tag worn-out proteins with a small protein label before the proteasome shreds them. What's my tag called?
A newborn's urine smells like maple syrup, and the infant is lethargic with poor feeding. Which enzyme complex is deficient?
explanation: This is maple syrup urine disease.

stem: A boy with gout, self-mutilating behavior, and choreoathetosis has a deficiency of which enzyme?
explanation: HGPRT deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.

stem: Fill in the blank: Zellweger syndrome results from a defect in ____ biogenesis, impairing very-long-chain fatty acid breakdown.
An infant with a doll-like face, hepatomegaly, severe fasting hypoglycemia, and lactic acidosis has which glycogen storage disease?
explanation: Von Gierke disease (type I) is glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency.

stem: I let exercising muscle export lactate to the liver, which turns it back into glucose to send back out. What cycle am I?
A sailor on a long voyage develops bleeding gums, poor wound healing, and corkscrew body hairs. Which vitamin is deficient?
explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.

stem: I leave red blood cells vulnerable to oxidative stress from fava beans, sulfa drugs, or infections, causing hemolysis with Heinz bodies. What enzyme am I missing?
Fill in the blank: homocystinuria most commonly results from a deficiency of ____ synthase, causing lens dislocation, marfanoid habitus, and thrombosis.
I shuttle long-chain fatty acids across the inner mitochondrial membrane so they can be broken down for energy. What am I?
Pellagra's classic triad includes dermatitis, diarrhea, and ____ — caused by niacin (B3) deficiency.
Fill in the blank: beta-oxidation of fatty acids occurs primarily within the ____.
I'm curved like a comma, I love rice-water stools, and a toxin that locks on cAMP is my calling card. What am I?
A throat swab grows gram-positive cocci in chains, with a wide, completely clear zone of hemolysis around each colony on blood agar. Likely organism?
explanation: Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A strep) is beta-hemolytic: a complete clear zone on blood agar.

stem: Charcot's triad for ascending cholangitis includes fever, jaundice, and ____.
A splenectomized patient develops rapidly progressive sepsis. Which three encapsulated organisms pose the highest risk and are targeted by post-splenectomy vaccination?
choices: S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae type b, and N. meningitidis
S. aureus, S. epidermidis, and Enterococcus
M. tuberculosis, M. avium, and M. leprae
C. difficile, C. perfringens, and C. tetani

stem: I'm the bacterium that hijacks the host cell's actin to rocket-propel myself cell-to-cell, dodging antibodies entirely — a particular risk in pregnancy and the immunocompromised. Who am I?
Fill in the blank: a ____ preparation using potassium hydroxide dissolves keratin to reveal fungal hyphae or yeast forms from a skin scraping.
A patient with night sweats, weight loss, and hemoptysis has bilateral upper-lobe cavitary lesions on chest imaging, confirmed by an acid-fast sputum stain. Which organism?
Congenital toxoplasmosis classically presents with chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, and ____.
I hide inside macrophages, cause a painless genital ulcer with painful, matted inguinal lymph nodes ("buboes"), and respond to doxycycline. What am I?
explanation: This is lymphogranuloma venereum, caused by C. trachomatis serovars L1–L3.

stem: A patient bitten by a tick develops an expanding bullseye rash, then weeks later facial nerve palsy and joint pain. Which spirochete is responsible?
explanation: Borrelia burgdorferi causes Lyme disease.

stem: A feverish child recovering from a viral illness is given aspirin, then develops vomiting, liver dysfunction, and encephalopathy. What is this called?
Whipple's triad for confirming true hypoglycemia includes symptoms consistent with low glucose, a documented low glucose level, and ____.
choices: Relief of symptoms after glucose administration

stem: I cause lockjaw and a fixed grinning expression called "risus sardonicus" by blocking inhibitory neurotransmitter release. What am I?
A positive urease breath test in a patient with peptic ulcers points to infection with which organism?
Eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions called Negri bodies, seen in neurons after an animal bite, confirm which infection?
Fill in the blank: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia becomes a major risk in HIV patients once the CD4 count falls below ____ cells/microliter.
A patient develops descending, symmetric flaccid paralysis with diplopia and dry mouth after eating home-canned food. Which toxin is responsible?
Which Plasmodium species causes the most severe, potentially fatal form of malaria due to its ability to sequester in small vessels?
Fill in the blank: untreated syphilis progresses through a primary painless chancre, a secondary disseminated rash, and a tertiary stage marked by ____.

A diabetic patient's leg wound spreads rapidly with severe pain out of proportion to exam findings, crepitus, and gray, foul-smelling tissue. Group A strep or polymicrobial infection causing this "flesh-eating" process is called?
I block the enzyme that converts angiotensin I to angiotensin II — a dry cough is my signature side effect. What drug class am I?
Anticholinergic toxicity is remembered as "hot as a hare, dry as a bone, red as a beet, mad as a hatter," and also ____.
A patient on warfarin presents with major bleeding. Which two interventions most rapidly reverse the anticoagulant effect?
choices: Vitamin K plus PCC or fresh frozen plasma

stem: Fill in the blank: the first-line drug class for terminating status epilepticus is ____.
I'm the competitive antagonist given to reverse opioid overdose by displacing the drug from mu receptors. What am I?
explanation: Naltrexone is a longer-acting oral antagonist used for maintenance, not acute overdose reversal.

stem: Serotonin syndrome's classic triad includes autonomic instability, altered mental status, and ____.
explanation: Neuromuscular abnormalities include clonus and hyperreflexia.

stem: Fill in the blank: methyldopa and labetalol are preferred antihypertensives in ____ due to their established safety profile.
I block dihydropteroate synthase, starving bacteria of folate they can't get from their diet like we can. What drug class am I?
A patient on a cardiac glycoside develops yellow-green visual halos and new arrhythmias. Which drug is responsible?
Fill in the blank: the antidote for acetaminophen overdose, which replenishes glutathione stores, is ____.
I'm the "silver bullet" for methanol or ethylene glycol poisoning, blocking alcohol dehydrogenase before toxic metabolites can form. What am I?
A patient on a lipid-lowering drug develops muscle pain, weakness, and dark urine. Which class is responsible for this rhabdomyolysis risk?
Fill in the blank: ____ is the competitive antagonist used to reverse benzodiazepine overdose or oversedation.
I'm nicknamed "angiotensin II's gatekeeper" because I block the final enzymatic step that produces a powerful vasoconstrictor. Which drug class fits this description?
Malignant hyperthermia's triad from triggering anesthetics includes severe hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, and ____.
Fill in the blank: tetracyclines are avoided in children and pregnancy because they cause ____.
choices: Tooth discoloration and bone growth inhibition

stem: A patient in anaphylaxis needs which drug as first-line treatment, given intramuscularly without delay?
I irreversibly block the proton pump on gastric parietal cells to reduce acid secretion. What drug class am I?
A psychiatric patient on long-term therapy develops a fine tremor, ataxia, and excessive dilute urination. Which drug is the likely cause?
Fill in the blank: giving glucagon can reverse severe toxicity from ____ overdose by bypassing the blocked receptor.
choices: Calcium channel blockers or beta blockers

stem: I'm a programmed, orderly form of cell death that doesn't trigger inflammation, unlike my messier cousin. What am I?
explanation: Pyknosis (nuclear shrinkage) is a feature of both apoptosis and necrosis, not a separate process.

stem: Virchow's triad for venous thrombosis includes stasis of blood flow, endothelial injury, and ____.
Large, binucleated cells with prominent nucleoli resembling "owl's eyes" are the diagnostic hallmark of which malignancy?
explanation: These are Reed-Sternberg cells.

stem: Fill in the blank: concentrically laminated calcified structures called ____ bodies are seen in papillary thyroid carcinoma, meningioma, and serous ovarian tumors.
The normal squamous epithelium of the lower esophagus is replaced by columnar epithelium due to chronic acid reflux. What is this reversible cellular adaptation called?
A granuloma with central necrotic, cheese-like debris is a hallmark of infection with which organism?
Fill in the blank: needle-like cytoplasmic inclusions called ____ rods are a diagnostic clue for acute myeloid leukemia.
Meigs syndrome classically presents with an ovarian fibroma, ascites, and ____.
Fill in the blank: large cells with a single, large, basophilic intranuclear inclusion — described as "____ eyes" — indicate cytomegalovirus infection.
Mucin-filled cells with a nucleus pushed to the periphery, giving them their name, are characteristic of which malignancy?
explanation: Signet ring cell adenocarcinoma most often arises in the stomach.

stem: Eosinophilic, round apoptotic bodies seen in hepatocytes during viral hepatitis are named after their discoverer. What are they called?
Fill in the blank: inherited mutations in ____ dramatically raise lifetime risk of breast and ovarian cancer.
Which term describes cells so disorganized and abnormal that their tissue of origin becomes difficult to identify — a hallmark of high-grade malignancy?
A lymph node biopsy shows sheets of medium-sized cells with a "starry sky" pattern from scattered macrophages. Which lymphoma is this?
A triangular area of periosteal elevation on X-ray, where a tumor lifts the periosteum away from bone, is called what — and is classically seen in which malignancy?
Beck's triad for cardiac tamponade includes hypotension, jugular venous distension, and ____.
explanation: Pulsus paradoxus is common in tamponade but is not part of Beck's triad.

stem: Fill in the blank: the p53 gene functions as a ____, halting the cell cycle or triggering apoptosis in response to DNA damage.
A reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22, producing the BCR-ABL fusion protein, is the hallmark of which leukemia?
explanation: The t(9;22) is the Philadelphia chromosome.

stem: A patient with severe burns develops a gastric or duodenal stress ulcer. What is this specific ulcer called, as distinguished from the one seen after severe brain injury?
Fill in the blank: amyloid deposits show apple-green birefringence under polarized light after staining with ____.
I'm the first antibody sent to the front lines of a new infection — five subunits joined as one giant pentamer. What am I?
DiGeorge syndrome's features include cardiac defects, hypocalcemia, and ____.
A patient eats shellfish and within minutes develops hives, wheezing, and swelling. Which hypersensitivity type is this?
Fill in the blank: MHC class I presents antigen to CD8+ T cells, while MHC class II presents to ____ T cells.
Think of me as the immune system's demolition crew — a cascade of proteins ending in a pore that punches holes in bacterial membranes. What am I?
explanation: The terminal pore is the membrane attack complex (C5b–C9).

stem: I kill virus-infected or tumor cells without needing prior sensitization or antigen presentation. What cell type am I?
An infant has recurrent severe infections from birth with absent T cells and B cells — described as needing a sterile "bubble" environment. What condition is this?
Fill in the blank: B cell class switching from IgM to other isotypes requires cytokine signals and binding of ____ on the helper T cell to CD40 on the B cell.
Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome's triad includes thrombocytopenia, recurrent infections, and ____.
A person previously stung by a bee is stung again and rapidly develops airway swelling and shock. What triggers this rapid reaction?
choices: Cross-linking of preformed IgE on mast cells
Direct toxin effect with no immune involvement

stem: I'm the immune system's peacekeeper, suppressing overactive immune responses and preventing autoimmunity. What cell type am I?
In Goodpasture syndrome, antibodies directly attack collagen in the kidney and lung basement membranes. Which hypersensitivity type is this?
explanation: Type II hypersensitivity is cytotoxic, antibody-mediated.

stem: Serum sickness, with fever, rash, and joint pain days after antitoxin administration, results from which hypersensitivity mechanism?
explanation: Immune complex deposition is type III hypersensitivity.

stem: A positive PPD skin test (tuberculin reaction), appearing 48-72 hours after injection, reflects which hypersensitivity type?
explanation: Type IV hypersensitivity is delayed and T-cell mediated.

stem: Fill in the blank: Bruton's (X-linked) agammaglobulinemia results from a defective ____ gene, leading to absent mature B cells.
explanation: BTK is Bruton tyrosine kinase.

stem: I'm the body's dedicated "antibody factory," a fully differentiated B cell that no longer divides but churns out one specific antibody. What am I?
Recurrent infections with catalase-positive organisms (like Staph aureus and Aspergillus), due to phagocytes that can't generate a respiratory burst, suggest which condition?
Fill in the blank: Hyper-IgM syndrome results from a defect in ____, preventing immunoglobulin class switching.
I'm a small signaling protein released by virus-infected cells, warning neighboring cells to raise their antiviral defenses. What am I?
After a bone marrow transplant, donor T cells attack the recipient's skin, gut, and liver. What is this complication called?
Job (Hyper-IgE) syndrome's classic triad includes eczema, recurrent skin/lung infections, and ____.
Fill in the blank: deficiency of terminal complement components C5-C9 predisposes specifically to recurrent infections with ____.
Which screening test is most commonly used to evaluate a patient for suspected systemic lupus erythematosus?
I directly kill infected or cancerous cells by releasing perforin and granzymes, recognizing antigen presented on MHC class I. What am I?
Fill in the blank: live attenuated vaccines are generally contraindicated in ____ patients due to the risk of causing actual disease.
I result from an extra copy of the smallest autosome, causing intellectual disability, a flat facial profile, and a single palmar crease. What am I?
DiGeorge (22q11.2 deletion) syndrome is remembered by "CATCH-22": Cardiac defects, Abnormal facies, Thymic aplasia, Cleft palate, and ____.
A boy has intellectual disability, a long face with large ears, and enlarged testes after puberty. Which trinucleotide repeat disorder is this?
Fill in the blank: Huntington disease results from expansion of a ____ trinucleotide repeat on chromosome 4.
I describe how trinucleotide repeat diseases tend to appear earlier and more severely in each successive generation. What phenomenon am I?
A tall male with gynecomastia, small testes, and infertility has an extra X chromosome. What karyotype does he have?
explanation: 47,XXY is Klinefelter syndrome.

stem: A short female with a webbed neck, wide-spaced nipples, and coarctation of the aorta has which karyotype?
explanation: 45,X is Turner syndrome.

stem: Fill in the blank: in autosomal dominant inheritance, an affected heterozygous parent has a ____ chance of passing the condition to each child.
choices: Depends only on the child's sex

stem: Marfan syndrome's classic triad includes tall stature with long limbs, lens dislocation, and ____.
A child has recurrent lung infections, pancreatic insufficiency, and abnormally salty sweat. A mutation in which gene, on which chromosome, is responsible?
I'm the only inheritance pattern where a father can never pass a condition to his children, but an affected mother passes it to all of hers. What pattern am I?

Fill in the blank: the same deleted region of chromosome 15 causes Prader-Willi syndrome if inherited from the father, or Angelman syndrome if inherited from the mother — a phenomenon called genomic ____.
A patient with germline mutations in the TP53 gene has dramatically elevated lifetime risk of multiple cancer types starting at a young age. What syndrome is this?
An infant has severe intellectual disability, rocker-bottom feet, clenched fists with overlapping fingers, and a small jaw, dying within the first year of life. Which trisomy is this?
explanation: Trisomy 18 is Edwards syndrome.

stem: Fill in the blank: Robertsonian translocations most commonly involve the acrocentric chromosomes, including chromosomes 13, 14, 15, 21, and ____.
A short-limbed dwarf with a normal-sized trunk and macrocephaly has a mutation in which gene, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern?
explanation: FGFR3 gain-of-function mutations cause achondroplasia.

stem: I'm the molecular tool made from a bacterial defense system, using a guide RNA to direct precise cuts in DNA. What am I?
A patient has multiple café-au-lait spots, axillary freckling, and soft skin tumors called neurofibromas. Which condition is this, and what type?
Fill in the blank: in autosomal recessive inheritance, two unaffected carrier parents have a ____ chance of having an affected child.
An Ashkenazi Jewish infant develops progressive neurodegeneration, an exaggerated startle response, and a cherry-red spot on macular exam. Which enzyme is deficient?
explanation: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease.

stem: Patau syndrome (trisomy 13) features cleft lip/palate, polydactyly, and ____.
Fill in the blank: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene and is inherited in an ____ pattern, affecting mostly boys.
What key clinical difference helps distinguish Klinefelter syndrome from Turner syndrome at the bedside?
choices: Klinefelter affects only females; Turner only males
Klinefelter patients are phenotypically male; Turner patients are phenotypically female
Turner syndrome causes tall stature; Klinefelter causes short stature
Klinefelter always causes infertility in females
Turner syndrome involves an extra X chromosome

stem: A condensed, inactivated X chromosome visible at the periphery of the nucleus in female somatic cells is called what?
Fill in the blank: genetic anticipation — worsening severity and earlier onset across generations — is classically seen in ____ disorders.
I'm a specialized cell in the intestinal and respiratory epithelium, shaped like my namesake, releasing protective mucus. What am I?
Chronic acid reflux causes the lower esophagus's normal squamous epithelium to be replaced by columnar epithelium. What is this condition called?
Fill in the blank: ____ cells, found at the base of small intestinal crypts, secrete antimicrobial peptides like defensins to protect intestinal stem cells.
I'm a large, multinucleated cell that dissolves bone matrix, working opposite the cells that build bone back up. What am I?
Which specialized epidermal cells act as mechanoreceptors, sensing light touch and pressure?
Fill in the blank: the zona glomerulosa, the outermost layer of the adrenal cortex, secretes ____.
explanation: The zona glomerulosa makes mineralocorticoids, chiefly aldosterone.

stem: Think of me as the cell's "mailroom" — proteins arrive from the ER to be modified, sorted, and shipped to their final destination. What organelle am I?
Which zone of the liver lobule, farthest from the portal triad and closest to the central vein, is most vulnerable to ischemia and toxin-related injury?
Which antigen-presenting cells reside in the epidermis, capturing antigens before migrating to lymph nodes?
Fill in the blank: type I pneumocytes are specialized for gas exchange, while type II pneumocytes produce ____.
I'm a gastric gland cell that secretes pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of a protein-digesting enzyme. What am I?
Autoimmune destruction of which gastric cells causes pernicious anemia by eliminating intrinsic factor production?
Fill in the blank: specialized cells surrounding the afferent arteriole, called ____ cells, sense low blood pressure and secrete renin.
explanation: Macula densa cells sense distal tubular NaCl; juxtaglomerular cells secrete renin.

stem: Think of me as the cell's power plant, generating ATP through oxidative phosphorylation. What organelle am I?
Myelin in the peripheral nervous system is produced by Schwann cells, while in the central nervous system it's produced by which cell type?
Which resident liver macrophages are responsible for clearing old red blood cells and pathogens from portal blood?
explanation: Pit cells are liver NK-like cells, not the main phagocytes.

stem: Fill in the blank: ____ cells in the testis support developing sperm cells and form the blood-testis barrier via tight junctions.
Which testicular cells, located in the interstitium, produce testosterone in response to LH?
Which specialized glomerular cells wrap around capillaries with foot processes (pedicels) to form the filtration slits?
Fill in the blank: the basal layer (stratum basale) of the epidermis is the primary site of ____ that continually renews the skin.
explanation: The stratum basale holds the stem cells that divide to renew the epidermis.

stem: A short signal sequence on a nascent protein acts like a molecular "postal code," directing it to the endoplasmic reticulum for further processing. What is this sequence called?
Coordinated beating of respiratory tract cilia sweeps mucus and trapped particles upward and out. Failure of this mechanism is seen in which genetic condition?
explanation: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (Kartagener syndrome when with situs inversus) causes bronchiectasis as a consequence.

stem: Kartagener syndrome's features include recurrent sinopulmonary infections, infertility, and ____.
Autoantibodies against which cell junction protein cause the flaccid, easily ruptured blisters of pemphigus vulgaris?
explanation: Pemphigus vulgaris targets desmoglein in desmosomes.

stem: I'm a connective tissue cell packed with granules of histamine and heparin, ready to degranulate during allergic reactions. What am I?
explanation: Basophils are the similar granulocyte in blood; mast cells live in tissue.

stem: Failure of the neural tube to fully close is responsible for a spectrum of conditions from anencephaly to which spinal condition?
A baby is born with a fully open skull and absent cerebral hemispheres. This is the most severe form of which developmental defect?
Fill in the blank: the neural tube gives rise to the entire ____.
explanation: The neural tube forms the brain and spinal cord.

stem: I'm a transient midline structure that induces overlying ectoderm to form the neural tube, later becoming the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral discs. What am I?
DiGeorge syndrome results from abnormal development of which paired embryonic structures?
Fill in the blank: the first pharyngeal arch gives rise to the muscles of mastication and the mandible, via a cartilage called ____ cartilage.
explanation: Reichert's cartilage and the hyoid are second-arch derivatives.

stem: The VACTERL association describes a nonrandom cluster of birth defects: Vertebral, Anal, Cardiac, Tracheoesophageal fistula, Renal, and ____.
I'm the structure that establishes the body's bilateral symmetry and gives rise to all three germ layers during early development. What am I?
Fill in the blank: the ectoderm germ layer gives rise to the epidermis and the entire ____.
Which germ layer gives rise to muscle, bone, blood vessels, and the kidneys?
explanation: Neural crest is a distinct ectoderm-derived cell population, not a primary germ layer.

stem: The lining of the gastrointestinal tract, liver, and lungs all originate from which germ layer?
Fill in the blank: failure of the fetal connection between the aorta and pulmonary artery to close after birth results in a ____.
Fetal circulation uses shunts like the ductus arteriosus and foramen ovale to bypass which organ that isn't yet needed for gas exchange?
Which fetal structure allows blood to shunt directly from the right atrium to the left atrium, bypassing the pulmonary circulation?
A newborn's abdominal organs protrude through a defect lateral to an intact umbilical cord, with no covering membrane. Is this omphalocele or gastroschisis?
choices: Neither — this describes an umbilical hernia

stem: Fill in the blank: a Meckel's diverticulum results from incomplete obliteration of the ____ duct.
The allantois, an embryonic structure connected to the bladder, normally regresses into which adult structure?
explanation: The allantois becomes the urachus, which obliterates into the median umbilical ligament.

stem: A fetus with bilateral renal agenesis produces too little amniotic fluid, leading to pulmonary hypoplasia and limb deformities. What is this sequence called?
Fill in the blank: persistence of the urachus after birth can lead to drainage of urine from the umbilicus, a condition called a ____.
Tetralogy of Fallot's four features are a ventricular septal defect, an overriding aorta, pulmonary stenosis, and ____.
The process by which the bilaminar embryonic disc becomes trilaminar, forming ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm, is called what?
A newborn lacks ganglion cells in the distal colon, causing severe constipation and megacolon. Failure of migration of which embryonic cells causes this?
Fill in the blank: neural crest cells migrate widely to form melanocytes, the adrenal medulla, and much of the ____ nervous system.
explanation: Neural crest forms sensory and autonomic ganglia, among other PNS structures.

stem: Identical twins who share one placenta but each have a separate amniotic sac result from division of the embryo at which timepoint?
explanation: Days 0-3: dichorionic diamniotic; 4-8: monochorionic diamniotic; 9-12: monoamniotic; 13+: conjoined twins.

stem: Fill in the blank: dizygotic (fraternal) twins always have ____ chorions and ____ amniotic sacs, since they arise from two separately fertilized eggs.
choices: It varies randomly regardless of fertilization

stem: I'm a blind-ended tube hanging off the cecum, once thought useless, now known to house gut bacteria for recolonization. What am I?
Fill in the blank: baroreceptors that sense blood pressure changes are located in the carotid sinus and the ____.
I'm stored as branched chains of glucose in the liver and muscle, ready to be broken down when blood sugar drops. What am I?
explanation: Amylopectin is the branched plant starch; glycogen is the human storage form.

stem: I mutate my surface proteins gradually year to year (drift), but occasionally swap whole gene segments for a pandemic-causing overhaul (shift). What virus am I?
I block beta-adrenergic receptors, slowing the heart rate and reducing blood pressure and myocardial oxygen demand. What drug class am I?
I'm the spread of cancer cells from their original site to a distant organ, usually via blood or lymphatics. What am I?
Fill in the blank: in ____ disease, the immune system mistakenly attacks the body's own healthy tissue as if it were foreign.
I'm caused by a single point mutation swapping one amino acid in the beta-globin chain, causing red cells to sickle under low oxygen. What am I?
Fill in the blank: hyaline, elastic, and ____ are the three types of cartilage found in the body.
I'm a ball of cells that burrows into the uterine lining about a week after fertilization, beginning pregnancy. What process am I?
I happen when you reject a true null hypothesis — concluding there's an effect when there really isn't one. What error am I?
I'm a dense structure inside the nucleus, not membrane-bound, where ribosomal subunits are assembled before export to the cytoplasm. What am I?
I sit below the cerebrum, coordinating balance, posture, and fine motor movement — damage to me causes ataxia and intention tremor. What am I?
Fill in the blank: the rotator cuff muscles, remembered by "SITS," are supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor, and ____.
Fill in the blank: renin converts angiotensinogen into angiotensin I, which is then converted by ACE into ____.
Fill in the blank: the rate-limiting, committed step of gluconeogenesis is catalyzed by fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase, opposing glycolysis's ____ enzyme.
Fill in the blank: a positive ____ on hepatitis B serology indicates active infection (either acute or chronic).
Fill in the blank: the first-line rescue medication for acute asthma symptoms is a short-acting ____ agonist, such as albuterol.
Fill in the blank: cancer staging using the TNM system evaluates tumor size, lymph ____ involvement, and distant metastasis.
Fill in the blank: rheumatoid factor is an antibody, usually IgM, directed against the ____ portion of IgG.
Fill in the blank: sickle cell anemia is inherited in an ____ pattern, requiring two copies of the mutant allele for disease.
Fill in the blank: bone remodeling relies on a triad of cells — bone-forming osteoblasts, mature osteocytes, and bone-resorbing ____.
explanation: Osteoclasts derive from the monocyte-macrophage lineage.

stem: Fill in the blank: human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), the hormone detected in pregnancy tests, is produced by the ____.
I happen when you fail to reject a false null hypothesis — missing a real effect that's actually there. What error am I?
Fill in the blank: DNA replication occurs during the ____ phase of the cell cycle, between the two gap phases.
Fill in the blank: ____ area, located in the inferior frontal gyrus, is responsible for speech production — damage causes non-fluent, effortful speech.
A patient with a fractured pelvis has weakness in hip flexion and numbness on the anterior thigh — which major nerve, formed from L2-L4, is likely injured?
A hospitalized patient develops severe hyponatremia with concentrated urine despite normal volume status, after starting a new antidepressant. Which condition is this?
explanation: SIADH (syndrome of inappropriate ADH) is a known side effect of SSRIs.

stem: A patient develops muscle cramps and dark urine (myoglobinuria) with strenuous exercise, but has normal blood glucose. Deficiency of which enzyme is likely?
explanation: Tarui disease (PFK deficiency) can look similar but McArdle disease is the classic answer.

stem: A hospitalized patient on antibiotics develops profuse watery diarrhea and pseudomembranes seen on colonoscopy. Which organism is responsible?
Which folate antagonist is used both in cancer chemotherapy and at lower doses for autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis?
Persistent, disordered cellular growth that hasn't yet invaded through the basement membrane, but shows abnormal size, shape, and organization, is called what?
A patient with fatigue, weight gain, and a firm, non-tender goiter has antibodies against thyroid peroxidase. What condition is this?
A patient of Mediterranean descent has microcytic anemia with target cells, but normal iron studies — deficient production of one globin chain. What condition is this?
Fill in the blank: the skin's three main layers, from superficial to deep, are the epidermis, dermis, and ____.
explanation: The hypodermis is the subcutaneous layer; the stratum corneum and papillary layer are sublayers.

stem: A woman has one-sided pelvic pain and vaginal bleeding at 6 weeks' gestation, with a positive pregnancy test but an empty uterus on ultrasound. Where does this pregnancy most commonly implant abnormally?
A study reports a p-value of 0.03 for its primary outcome. Using the conventional threshold, how should this result be interpreted?
choices: Proof the null hypothesis is true

stem: I'm nicknamed the "guardian of the genome" — sensing DNA damage, I halt the cell cycle or trigger apoptosis to prevent mutated cells from dividing. What gene product am I?
A patient can speak fluently but the words are nonsensical, and they can't understand spoken language. Damage to which brain area causes this?
Fill in the blank: the brachial plexus arises from spinal nerve roots ____.
Fill in the blank: in central diabetes insipidus, a deficiency of ____ leads to excessive dilute urine output.
explanation: ADH is also called vasopressin.

stem: Fill in the blank: the citric acid (Krebs) cycle takes place within the ____ of the cell.
Fill in the blank: lancet-shaped, gram-positive diplococci are the classic microscopic appearance of ____, the most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia.
Fill in the blank: the antidote used to reverse heparin's anticoagulant effect is ____.
Fill in the blank: the four major types of necrosis are coagulative, liquefactive, fat, and ____.
explanation: Apoptosis is programmed cell death, not necrosis.

stem: Fill in the blank: in Graves' disease, autoantibodies bind to and stimulate the ____, causing hyperthyroidism.
Fill in the blank: hereditary hemochromatosis, causing iron overload affecting the liver, heart, and pancreas, is most commonly linked to mutations in the ____ gene.
Fill in the blank: the three types of muscle tissue are skeletal, cardiac, and ____.
Fill in the blank: the placenta is formed from fetal tissue (chorion) and maternal tissue called the ____.
Fill in the blank: ____ measures the proportion of people with a disease who correctly test positive — a test's ability to catch true cases.
Fill in the blank: the four phases of mitosis, in order, are prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and ____.
Fill in the blank: the ____ is the thick bundle of nerve fibers connecting the left and right cerebral hemispheres.
explanation: The anterior commissure is a much smaller interhemispheric connection.

stem: I'm the longest cranial nerve, wandering far beyond the head and neck to supply parasympathetic innervation to the heart, lungs, and most of the gut. What am I?
I'm the anabolic hormone released by pancreatic beta cells, driving glucose into cells and lowering blood sugar after a meal. What am I?
I read the template DNA strand and proofread as I go, synthesizing a new strand in the 5' to 3' direction. What enzyme am I?
I'm a retrovirus that uses reverse transcriptase to convert my RNA genome into DNA before integrating into the host cell. What am I?
In diabetic ketoacidosis, which hormone is administered intravenously to lower blood glucose and shift potassium into cells?
I'm the pink, granular tissue made of new capillaries and fibroblasts that fills in a healing wound before scar formation. What am I?
Fill in the blank: ____ vaccines use an inactivated bacterial toxin to generate protective antibodies, as used for tetanus and diphtheria.
A patient develops liver cirrhosis, diabetes, and bronze-colored skin from iron deposition in multiple organs. Mutation in which gene is responsible?
I'm a biconcave disc with no nucleus and no mitochondria, built entirely around carrying oxygen. What cell am I?
I connect the fetus to the placenta, normally containing two arteries carrying deoxygenated blood away from the fetus and one vein carrying oxygenated blood to it. What am I?
A patient's symptoms improve after taking an inert sugar pill they believed was real medication. What phenomenon explains this?
I cap the ends of your chromosomes, protecting them from degradation and fusion, but I shorten with each cell division — a molecular clock for aging. What am I?
I'm a curved structure deep in the temporal lobe, essential for forming new long-term memories — damage to me (as in patient H.M.) causes anterograde amnesia. What am I?
A patient develops hoarseness after thyroid surgery. Which nerve was most likely injured?
explanation: External superior laryngeal nerve injury affects voice pitch; recurrent laryngeal nerve injury causes hoarseness.

stem: Fill in the blank: ____ is the counter-regulatory hormone released by pancreatic alpha cells, raising blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis.
A child with severe sun sensitivity and early skin cancers has a defect in nucleotide excision repair. What condition is this?
An immunocompromised patient develops white, curd-like plaques in the mouth that scrape off, revealing red mucosa underneath. Which organism is responsible?
A patient who took too much aspirin presents with tinnitus, hyperventilation, and a mixed acid-base disturbance. Which acid-base pattern is classically seen first?
choices: Isolated hyperkalemia with no acid-base change
explanation: Salicylates first stimulate respiration (respiratory alkalosis), then an anion gap metabolic acidosis follows.

stem: Which raised, excessive scar extends beyond the original wound margins and is more common in darker-skinned individuals, distinguishing it from a hypertrophic scar?
Which autoimmune blistering disease is caused by antibodies against desmoglein, producing flaccid, easily ruptured blisters, as opposed to the tense blisters of its counterpart?
A patient with liver disease, psychiatric symptoms, and golden-brown rings around the cornea has copper accumulating due to a mutation in which gene?
explanation: ATP7B mutations cause Wilson disease.

stem: Which immature red blood cells, still containing residual RNA, increase in number as a marker of active bone marrow response to anemia or blood loss?
An infant is born with a single umbilical artery instead of the usual two. This finding should raise suspicion for what?
choices: Maternal diabetes as the only possible cause
explanation: A single umbilical artery is linked to renal and cardiac anomalies.

stem: Fill in the blank: the number needed to treat (NNT) represents how many patients must receive a treatment for one additional patient to ____.
explanation: NNT = 1 / absolute risk reduction.

stem: Fill in the blank: cancer cells often reactivate the enzyme ____, which rebuilds chromosome-end sequences and grants them limitless replicative potential.
Loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, part of the basal ganglia circuit, causes resting tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia. What condition is this?
Fill in the blank: the scalp's layers, from superficial to deep, are remembered by "SCALP" — skin, connective tissue, aponeurosis, loose connective tissue, and ____.
explanation: The P in SCALP stands for pericranium, the periosteum of the skull.

stem: Fill in the blank: the renal tubule runs from the renal corpuscle through the proximal tubule, loop of Henle, and distal tubule, then drains directly into the ____.
explanation: The collecting duct is not strictly part of the nephron; it has a separate embryologic origin.

stem: Fill in the blank: amino acids the body cannot synthesize and must obtain from the diet are called ____ amino acids.
Fill in the blank: E. coli O157:H7 produces a Shiga-like toxin that can cause bloody diarrhea and progress to ____.
Fill in the blank: patients with a true penicillin allergy have some risk of cross-reactivity with ____, particularly earlier-generation ones.
Fill in the blank: fluid that leaks out due to increased hydrostatic pressure, low in protein, is called a ____, as opposed to a protein-rich exudate from inflammation.
Fill in the blank: ____ are the white blood cells most elevated in parasitic infections and allergic reactions, identifiable by their bilobed nucleus and red-orange granules.
A patient with progressive dyspnea and progressive liver cirrhosis has panacinar emphysema at a young age. Which condition, inherited in an autosomal recessive/codominant pattern, is this?
Fill in the blank: unlike skeletal and smooth muscle, cardiac muscle cells are connected end-to-end by specialized junctions called ____, allowing coordinated contraction.
Fill in the blank: the drug ____, once prescribed for morning sickness, is a classic teratogen causing severe limb reduction defects (phocomelia).
Fill in the blank: positive predictive value — the chance a positive test result truly reflects disease — rises as disease ____ in the tested population increases.
Fill in the blank: genetic information flows from DNA to RNA via transcription in the ____, and from RNA to protein via translation in the ____.
Fill in the blank: the basal ganglia include the caudate nucleus, putamen, and ____.
explanation: The substantia nigra and subthalamic nucleus are functionally linked to the basal ganglia.

stem: I innervate the perineum, carrying sensation from the genitals and controlling the external urethral and anal sphincters. What am I?
I'm the coordinated, wave-like muscular contractions that push food through the digestive tract. What am I?
I bind to a receptor with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity, triggering a signaling cascade that moves glucose transporters to the cell surface. What hormone am I?
explanation: Growth hormone signals through a JAK-STAT cytokine receptor, not an intrinsic receptor tyrosine kinase.

stem: Reactivation of latent virus in the dorsal root ganglia, decades after childhood chickenpox, causes a painful, dermatomal vesicular rash. What is this called?
explanation: Herpes zoster is shingles.

stem: I'm the first-line oral medication for type 2 diabetes, primarily working by reducing hepatic glucose production. What am I?
Fatty streaks and fibrous plaques build up in arterial walls over decades, eventually risking rupture and thrombosis. What is this process called?
explanation: Atherosclerosis is one form of arteriosclerosis, the broader term.

stem: Which structure trains developing T cells to distinguish self from non-self?
Multiple fluid-filled cysts progressively replace kidney tissue, often with associated liver cysts and berry aneurysms, in a condition usually caused by PKD1 or PKD2 mutations. What is this?
Fill in the blank: ____ tissue, found in newborns and around organs, is metabolically active and generates heat through uncoupled mitochondrial respiration, unlike its white counterpart.
A newborn has small eyes, a thin upper lip, a smooth philtrum, and growth restriction after in-utero exposure to a common teratogen. What is this condition?
Fill in the blank: in a ____ study design, neither the participant nor the researcher knows who is receiving the active treatment versus placebo, minimizing bias.
I'm a membrane-bound organelle packed with digestive enzymes, breaking down cellular debris and worn-out organelles — nicknamed the cell's "suicide bag" if I rupture. What am I?
I sit between the cerebral cortex and the brainstem, relaying nearly all sensory information (except smell) on its way to conscious processing. What am I?
A fall onto an outstretched hand results in a "dinner fork" deformity of the wrist. Which fracture is this?
explanation: Colles is a dorsally displaced distal radius fracture; Smith is volar displacement.

stem: Which stomach cells, stimulated by protein-rich meals, secrete a hormone that in turn stimulates parietal cells to produce acid?
explanation: G cells secrete gastrin; ECL cells respond to gastrin by releasing histamine.

stem: A patient accumulates phytanic acid due to an inability to break down this branched-chain fatty acid, causing night blindness and peripheral neuropathy. What condition is this?
A college student develops fever, severe sore throat, and swollen lymph nodes, with atypical lymphocytes on blood smear. Which virus is the likely cause?
explanation: CMV can cause a similar mononucleosis picture, usually without marked pharyngitis.

stem: A patient on treatment for tuberculosis develops numbness and tingling in the feet. Which drug is responsible, and what vitamin prevents this side effect?
explanation: Vitamin B6 is pyridoxine.

stem: Thrombosis of the hepatic veins leads to painful hepatomegaly, ascites, and abdominal pain. What is this condition called?
explanation: Veno-occlusive disease affects the small hepatic venules rather than the hepatic veins.

stem: A patient with chronic diarrhea, weight loss, and iron deficiency has antibodies against tissue transglutaminase, improving on a gluten-free diet. What condition is this?

A patient develops hundreds to thousands of colon polyps starting in adolescence, with near-certain progression to colorectal cancer if untreated, due to a mutation in the APC gene. What condition is this?
explanation: Gardner syndrome is an FAP variant with extracolonic features.

stem: Fill in the blank: acetylcholine released at the ____ triggers depolarization of the adjacent skeletal muscle fiber.
Fill in the blank: maternal supplementation with ____ before and during early pregnancy reduces the risk of neural tube defects.
explanation: Excess vitamin A is teratogenic.

stem: The Kübler-Ross model of grief includes denial, anger, bargaining, and acceptance, alongside a fifth stage of ____.
Fill in the blank: I-cell disease results from failure to tag lysosomal enzymes with ____, so they're secreted outside the cell instead of delivered to lysosomes.

A stab wound causes hemisection of the spinal cord. The patient loses motor function and proprioception on the same side as the injury, but pain and temperature sensation on the opposite side. What is this syndrome?
Fill in the blank: the rotator cuff tendon most commonly torn, especially with age or repetitive overhead motion, is the ____.
Fill in the blank: ____, produced mainly by the kidney in response to low oxygen, stimulates red blood cell production in the bone marrow.
Fill in the blank: ____ reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis and the target of statin medications.
Fill in the blank: ____ is a gram-negative diplococcus that causes a purulent sexually transmitted infection and can also cause septic arthritis.
Fill in the blank: the chemotherapy agent ____ is well known for its dose-dependent cardiotoxicity, monitored with periodic echocardiograms.
explanation: Bleomycin is classically pulmonary toxic.

stem: Fill in the blank: a red (hemorrhagic) infarct typically occurs in organs with dual blood supply or loose tissue, such as the lung, while a white (pale) infarct occurs in solid organs with a single end-arterial supply, such as the ____.
explanation: The brain undergoes liquefactive necrosis after infarction.

stem: Fill in the blank: type 1 diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of pancreatic ____ cells, which normally produce insulin.

Fill in the blank: ____ syndrome results from inherited mutations in DNA mismatch repair genes, dramatically increasing risk of colorectal and endometrial cancer without the extensive polyps seen in FAP.

Fill in the blank: the anterior pituitary develops from oral ectoderm (Rathke's pouch) and produces hormones under hypothalamic control, while the posterior pituitary is actually an extension of the ____ that simply stores and releases hormones made elsewhere.
explanation: The posterior pituitary is neural tissue.

stem: Fill in the blank: cleft lip results from failure of fusion between the medial nasal process and the ____ process.
Fill in the blank: valid informed consent requires that a patient understands the diagnosis, the proposed treatment, its risks and benefits, and available ____.
explanation: Alternatives include no treatment.

stem: Fill in the blank: oxygen and small nonpolar molecules cross the cell membrane by simple ____, requiring no transport protein or energy.
explanation: Facilitated diffusion needs a channel or carrier; osmosis refers to water.

stem: Fill in the blank: anterior spinal artery occlusion causes bilateral motor loss and loss of pain/temperature sensation, but classically spares the ____, preserving vibration and proprioception.
Fill in the blank: the diaphragm's motor innervation comes from the phrenic nerve, roots C3, C4, and C5 — remembered as "____ keep the diaphragm alive."
I'm the heart's natural pacemaker, located in the right atrium, setting the intrinsic rhythm faster than any other cardiac tissue. What am I?
I'm a fat-soluble vitamin required to activate several clotting factors in the liver — my absorption is blocked by warfarin's mechanism of action. What am I?
I'm not a virus, bacterium, or fungus at all — just a misfolded protein that induces normal proteins to misfold too, riddling the brain with holes. What am I?
Fill in the blank: ____ medications reduce inflammation and suppress the immune system by mimicking cortisol, but long-term use risks osteoporosis and adrenal suppression.
Fill in the blank: excessive but organizationally normal cell proliferation, such as the endometrial lining thickening in response to estrogen, is called ____.
A patient with dry eyes, dry mouth, and joint pain has antibodies against Ro (SSA) and La (SSB) antigens. What condition is this?
A patient develops multiple hemangioblastomas of the retina and cerebellum along with renal cell carcinomas, due to a mutation in a tumor suppressor gene. What syndrome is this?

Fill in the blank: the anterior and posterior pituitary gland, though joined, have different embryologic origins and hormone production — the anterior pituitary produces its own hormones, while the posterior pituitary only ____.
choices: Stores and releases hormones made in the hypothalamus
Functions identically to the anterior lobe

stem: Fill in the blank: ____ is a congenital condition where the abdominal and thoracic organs are mirror-imaged compared to their normal position, often linked to ciliary dysfunction.
explanation: Dextrocardia refers to the heart alone; heterotaxy is a disordered rather than mirrored arrangement.

stem: I'm the systematic error that occurs when participants in a retrospective study inaccurately remember or report past exposures, especially if they already have the disease being studied. What bias am I?
I'm the enzyme pump that actively moves 3 sodium ions out of the cell for every 2 potassium ions it brings in, using ATP and maintaining the resting membrane potential. What am I?
Fill in the blank: the reticular activating system, located in the brainstem, is essential for maintaining ____ and arousal.
A weightlifter feels a sudden pop in the upper arm, followed by bulging of the muscle belly closer to the elbow — a "Popeye" deformity. Rupture of which tendon caused this?
Fill in the blank: during the strain phase of the Valsalva maneuver, venous return and cardiac output ____, followed by a reflex tachycardia.
Fill in the blank: deficiency of ____, a B-vitamin cofactor for carboxylase enzymes, is rare but can occur with excessive raw egg white consumption due to a binding protein called avidin.
An immunocompromised patient's chest CT shows a fungal mass with a surrounding air crescent within a pre-existing lung cavity. Which organism is this?
Fill in the blank: ____ are considered first-line pharmacologic treatment for major depressive disorder, working by blocking serotonin reuptake.
Fill in the blank: noncaseating granulomas in the lungs and lymph nodes, often with elevated ACE levels, are the hallmark of ____.
explanation: GPA has necrotizing granulomas; berylliosis can mimic sarcoidosis with noncaseating granulomas.

stem: Fill in the blank: deficiency of complement components C3 predisposes patients to recurrent, severe ____ infections.
Fill in the blank: patients with ____ syndrome have hypermobile joints, stretchy skin, and easy bruising, due to defective collagen structure.
Fill in the blank: the anterior pituitary is regulated by releasing and inhibiting hormones traveling through the ____ system from the hypothalamus.
Fill in the blank: a congenital diaphragmatic hernia most commonly occurs through the posterolateral ____ foramen, allowing abdominal contents into the thorax.
A researcher identifies a group of patients with lung cancer and a group without it, then looks backward to compare their smoking histories. What type of study design is this?
Fill in the blank: nondisjunction — failure of homologous chromosomes to separate properly — during meiosis is the most common cause of ____ syndrome.
explanation: Down syndrome (trisomy 21) most often results from maternal meiotic nondisjunction.

stem: A patient develops ascending, symmetric weakness and areflexia over days, weeks after a diarrheal illness, with elevated CSF protein but normal cell count. What condition is this?
Fill in the blank: compression of the ulnar nerve at the elbow, in the ____ tunnel, causes numbness in the ring and little fingers, worse with prolonged elbow flexion.
Fill in the blank: pulmonary surfactant, which reduces alveolar surface tension and prevents collapse, is produced by type ____ pneumocytes.
Fill in the blank: DNA and RNA bases are divided into purines (adenine and guanine) and pyrimidines (cytosine, thymine, and ____).
Fill in the blank: ____ is a flagellated protozoan causing foul-smelling, greasy diarrhea after ingestion of contaminated water, diagnosed by finding cysts or trophozoites in stool.
Fill in the blank: common opioid side effects include respiratory depression, sedation, and ____, which does not develop tolerance and often requires ongoing management.
Fill in the blank: elevated CA-125 is a tumor marker associated with ____ cancer, while elevated PSA is associated with prostate cancer.
Fill in the blank: deficiency of complement components C5 through C9 (the membrane attack complex) predisposes specifically to recurrent ____ infections.
Fill in the blank: osteogenesis imperfecta, or "brittle bone disease," most commonly results from mutations in ____ genes, impairing type I collagen production.
Fill in the blank: epithelial tissue is classified by cell shape (squamous, cuboidal, columnar) and by layering — a single layer is called simple, while multiple layers are called ____.
explanation: Pseudostratified epithelium is actually a single layer; transitional is one specific stratified type.

stem: Fill in the blank: the ____ gene, located on the Y chromosome, triggers the indifferent gonad to develop into a testis rather than an ovary.
explanation: SOX9 acts downstream of SRY.

stem: A researcher enrolls a group of currently healthy smokers and non-smokers, then follows them forward in time to see who develops lung cancer. What type of study design is this?
Fill in the blank: the rough endoplasmic reticulum, studded with ribosomes, specializes in synthesizing proteins for secretion, while the smooth endoplasmic reticulum specializes in ____.
Fill in the blank: the circle of Willis provides collateral blood flow to the brain, connected by the anterior communicating artery and the paired ____ communicating arteries.
Fill in the blank: under U.S. federal law (HIPAA), a patient's medical information is protected and generally cannot be shared without their ____.
Fill in the blank: apoptosis is carried out by a family of protease enzymes called ____, which cleave key cellular proteins in a controlled, orderly fashion.
A patient develops fluctuating muscle weakness that worsens with repeated activity and improves with rest, along with drooping eyelids. Autoantibodies against which receptor cause this?
explanation: This is myasthenia gravis; antibodies to voltage-gated calcium channels cause Lambert-Eaton syndrome instead.

stem: Fill in the blank: relative risk is calculated directly in cohort studies, while ____ is used as an approximation of relative risk in case-control studies, where the true incidence can't be measured.
I organize the mitotic spindle fibers that pull duplicated chromosomes apart during cell division, typically found in pairs near the nucleus. What am I?
Fill in the blank: multiple sclerosis is an autoimmune disease causing demyelination of the central nervous system, often detectable by ____ found on CSF analysis.
Fill in the blank: ____ occurs when a third, unmeasured factor independently influences both the exposure and the outcome, distorting the apparent relationship between them.
Fill in the blank: ____ are membrane-bound organelles that break down very-long-chain fatty acids and detoxify harmful substances like hydrogen peroxide.

Fill in the blank: a rapidly expanding mass above the tentorium can push the medial temporal lobe downward, compressing cranial nerve III against the tentorial edge and causing a fixed, dilated pupil — a process called ____ herniation.
Fill in the blank: recognizing that a screening test appears to prolong survival simply because it detects disease earlier — without actually changing the date of death — is called ____ bias.
Fill in the blank: multiple sclerosis classically causes ____, a syndrome of painful vision loss in one eye due to demyelination of the optic nerve.
explanation: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia is also seen in MS but is an eye-movement disorder, not vision loss.

stem: I make you drink constantly, urinate constantly, and eat constantly — yet you're still losing weight, because your cells can't use the sugar flooding your blood. What am I?
explanation: Polyuria, polydipsia and polyphagia with weight loss despite eating is the classic type 1 picture.

stem: A patient has fatigue, hypotension, and darkened skin creases, with low cortisol and high ACTH. What condition is this?
explanation: Addison's disease is primary adrenal insufficiency: low cortisol with high ACTH.

stem: Fill in the blank: the most common cause of Cushing syndrome overall is ____.
Reactive arthritis is remembered as "can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree," describing conjunctivitis, urethritis, and ____.
A patient has bulging eyes, an enlarged thyroid, weight loss, and a racing heart. What is the most likely underlying cause?
A patient reports fatigue, weight gain, constipation, and cold intolerance, with a slow heart rate on exam. Which condition fits best?
Fill in the blank: a malar ("butterfly") rash and a positive ANA test are classic supportive findings for ____.
Chronic kidney disease is staged primarily based on which measurement?
I cause heavy proteinuria, swelling, low blood albumin, and high cholesterol — all from a leaky glomerular filter. What syndrome am I?
Fill in the blank: nephritic syndrome classically presents with hematuria, hypertension, and ____.
explanation: Massive proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, hyperlipidemia and lipiduria point to nephrotic syndrome.

stem: A patient has fatigue, pale conjunctivae, and small, pale red blood cells with low ferritin on labs. Which type of anemia is this?
I cause large, oval red blood cells along with numbness, tingling, and gait problems from spinal cord involvement. What deficiency am I?
explanation: Folate deficiency causes a similar megaloblastic anemia but without neurologic signs.

stem: Fill in the blank: the majority of peptic ulcer disease cases are caused by infection with ____.
A patient has recurrent heartburn and a sour taste in the mouth, worse when lying down after meals. What condition is this?
Sudden, excruciating pain in the big toe, worse at night, from needle-shaped crystals depositing in the joint — what is this called?
Fill in the blank: pseudogout is caused by deposition of ____ crystals in the joint, as opposed to the urate crystals of true gout.
A patient has symmetric pain and stiffness in the small joints of both hands, worse in the morning and lasting over an hour. What condition fits best?
A young man has chronic low back pain and stiffness that improves with activity, eventually leading to a fused, "bamboo" spine on X-ray. Which HLA type is strongly associated?
Fill in the blank: unlike asthma, ____ is characterized by airflow obstruction that is largely irreversible even after bronchodilator therapy.
explanation: Pulmonary fibrosis is restrictive, not obstructive.

stem: A patient develops sudden shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain, and tachycardia after a long flight. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Unilateral leg swelling, warmth, and tenderness along the calf after prolonged immobility suggest what diagnosis?
Fill in the blank: anemia of chronic disease is typically normocytic, with a ____ ferritin level (distinguishing it from iron deficiency).
Fill in the blank: the most common underlying cause of hyperthyroidism is ____.
A patient with a long history of heavy alcohol use develops greasy, foul-smelling stools, new-onset diabetes, and pancreatic calcifications on imaging. What condition is this?
Fill in the blank: metabolic syndrome is diagnosed using a cluster of findings including abdominal obesity, elevated blood pressure, elevated fasting glucose, and abnormal ____ levels.
explanation: The lipid criteria are high triglycerides and low HDL.

stem: Crushing, vice-like chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw, with sweating and nausea — what am I describing?
Fill in the blank: ST-segment ____ on ECG, along with elevated troponin, defines a STEMI (ST-elevation myocardial infarction).
What key laboratory finding distinguishes NSTEMI from unstable angina, since both can show similar ECG changes?
choices: Elevated troponin in NSTEMI, elevated troponin in unstable angina
Elevated troponin in NSTEMI, normal troponin in unstable angina
Elevated white count in NSTEMI only

stem: Chest pain and pericardial friction rub developing one to several weeks after a myocardial infarction suggest which autoimmune-mediated complication?
An ECG shows no discernible P waves and an irregularly irregular rhythm. What arrhythmia is this?
Fill in the blank: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome is characterized by a short PR interval and a slurred initial upstroke of the QRS called a ____ wave.
Fill in the blank: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction reflects impaired systolic contraction, while heart failure with preserved ejection fraction reflects impaired ____.
A crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur that radiates to the carotid arteries, along with exertional syncope, suggests which valve lesion?
A holosystolic murmur best heard at the apex, radiating to the axilla, suggests which valve lesion?
Fill in the blank: mitral stenosis classically produces an opening snap followed by a diastolic rumble, most often as a late complication of ____.
Painless, flat, red macules on the palms and soles, along with tender nodules on the fingertips, are seen in which condition?
explanation: These are Janeway lesions (painless) and Osler nodes (tender).

stem: Rheumatic fever, following untreated strep throat, is diagnosed using the Jones criteria — which includes carditis, arthritis, and which skin/neurologic findings?
A young, otherwise healthy athlete collapses and dies suddenly during exertion. Autopsy reveals asymmetric septal hypertrophy. What condition caused this?
Fill in the blank: leg pain that occurs reliably with walking and resolves with rest, due to atherosclerotic narrowing of leg arteries, is called ____.
explanation: Claudication is the classic symptom of peripheral artery disease.

stem: Sudden, tearing chest pain radiating straight through to the back, with unequal blood pressures between arms, suggests which emergency?
Fill in the blank: coarctation of the aorta classically causes upper extremity hypertension along with ____ femoral pulses.
Sharp, pleuritic chest pain that improves when leaning forward, along with a friction rub on auscultation, suggests which condition?
Fill in the blank: prolongation of the QT interval increases risk of a dangerous polymorphic ventricular tachycardia called ____.
A patient has recurrent syncope and an ECG showing a coved ST-segment elevation in the right precordial leads, with a family history of sudden cardiac death. What condition is this?
A patient in shock has cold, clammy extremities, hypotension, and pulmonary edema after a large myocardial infarction. What is this called?
Fill in the blank: varicose veins result from incompetent venous ____, allowing blood to pool and reflux in superficial leg veins.
Fill in the blank: the CHA2DS2-VASc score is used to estimate ____ risk in patients with atrial fibrillation, guiding anticoagulation decisions.
Fill in the blank: cardiac tamponade causes an exaggerated drop in systolic blood pressure during inspiration, called pulsus ____.
A patient has episodes of extreme bradycardia alternating with tachycardia, often requiring a pacemaker. What condition is this?
Fill in the blank: in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, ACE inhibitors improve outcomes primarily by reducing ____.
explanation: ACE inhibitors block RAAS activation, reducing afterload and adverse remodeling.

stem: Pain that starts around the belly button and migrates to the lower right abdomen, worsening with movement, is classic for what?
A patient has right upper quadrant pain that worsens with inspiration during palpation under the rib margin. What is this exam finding called, and what does it suggest?
The classic triad for a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm includes hypotension, back pain, and ____.
Abdominal distension, vomiting, and inability to pass gas or stool point to which condition?
Fill in the blank: a femoral hernia protrudes below the inguinal ligament and is more common in ____, unlike the more common inguinal hernia.
Compartment syndrome's classic warning signs include pain out of proportion to injury, along with the "5 P's": pain, pallor, paresthesia, pulselessness, and ____.
A teenage boy has sudden, severe testicular pain, with the affected testicle riding high and an absent cremasteric reflex. What is the surgical emergency?
A segment of bowel twists on its own mesentery, cutting off blood supply — most commonly affecting the sigmoid colon in elderly patients. What is this called?
Left lower quadrant pain, fever, and a change in bowel habits in an older adult suggest inflammation of small outpouchings in the colon wall. What condition is this?
Fill in the blank: rebound tenderness and abdominal rigidity on exam suggest ____, often from a perforated viscus.
Fill in the blank: the "rule of nines" is used clinically to estimate the percentage of total body surface area affected by ____.
A diabetic patient develops rapidly spreading, severe genital and perineal pain with skin necrosis and crepitus. What surgical emergency is this?
Fill in the blank: unlike external hemorrhoids, ____ hemorrhoids are usually painless and located above the dentate line.
Sudden severe low back pain, saddle anesthesia, and new urinary retention or incontinence in a patient with a large disc herniation suggest which surgical emergency?
An elderly patient with atrial fibrillation develops sudden, severe abdominal pain that seems out of proportion to a fairly benign abdominal exam. What vascular emergency should be suspected?
Severe chest pain after forceful vomiting, with subcutaneous emphysema, suggests full-thickness rupture of which structure?
explanation: Full-thickness esophageal rupture after vomiting is Boerhaave syndrome.

stem: Fill in the blank: a Mallory-Weiss tear is a ____-thickness mucosal tear from forceful vomiting, unlike the full-thickness rupture of Boerhaave syndrome.
An infant develops "currant jelly" stools and episodes of drawing the knees to the chest, with a sausage-shaped mass on abdominal exam. What condition is this?
A firstborn male infant develops forceful, projectile, non-bilious vomiting after feeds, with a palpable olive-shaped mass in the abdomen. What condition is this?
Reynold's pentad, seen in severe ascending cholangitis, adds hypotension and altered mental status to Charcot's triad of fever, jaundice, and ____.
Fill in the blank: risk factors for gallstones are classically remembered as the "4 F's" — female, forty, fertile, and ____.
A gallstone erodes through the gallbladder wall into the small bowel, then obstructs the intestine further downstream. What is this rare complication called?
Fill in the blank: the primary survey in trauma follows the sequence airway, breathing, circulation, disability, and ____.
A trauma patient has tracheal deviation, absent breath sounds on one side, distended neck veins, and hypotension. What immediate intervention is needed?
Fill in the blank: pilonidal disease typically presents as a painful abscess or sinus tract in the ____ region.
explanation: Pilonidal disease occurs in the natal cleft.

stem: A child has had fever for five days, along with red eyes, a rash, a strawberry tongue, and swollen, peeling hands. What condition is this, and what serious complication is feared?
A toddler has a harsh, barking cough, hoarseness, and inspiratory stridor, worse at night. Which virus is the classic cause?
explanation: This is croup, classically caused by parainfluenza virus.

stem: A child appears toxic, drooling, and sits leaning forward in a "tripod" position, with a muffled voice and high fever. Which airway emergency is this, and what organism classically causes it?
Wheezing and respiratory distress in an infant during winter, caused by RSV infection of the small airways, describes which condition?
A premature infant develops bloody stools, abdominal distension, and gas seen within the bowel wall on X-ray. What condition is this?
A child consistently falls below expected growth curves for weight and height despite adequate caloric availability. What is this broadly called?
Fill in the blank: a child with persistent difficulty with social communication, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors starting early in development may be diagnosed with ____.
Fill in the blank: ADHD is characterized by a persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning, present in ____ or more settings.
Fill in the blank: cystic fibrosis in a newborn can present with a bowel obstruction called ____, caused by abnormally thick meconium.
Fill in the blank: congenital hypothyroidism is screened for at birth because untreated cases can cause irreversible ____.
An infant develops several days of high fever that suddenly resolves, followed by the appearance of a rose-pink rash. What condition is this?
A child develops a bright red rash on both cheeks, described as looking "slapped," caused by parvovirus B19. What is this condition called?
explanation: Erythema infectiosum is also known as fifth disease.

stem: Fill in the blank: measles is classically remembered by the "three C's" — cough, coryza, and ____ — along with pathognomonic Koplik spots.
Painful swelling of the parotid glands, sometimes with associated orchitis in post-pubertal males, is characteristic of which viral infection?
Fill in the blank: varicella (chickenpox) is characterized by vesicular lesions in ____ stages of healing appearing simultaneously across the body.
Vesicles on the palms, soles, and inside the mouth in a young child are classic for which viral infection?
explanation: Hand-foot-mouth disease is caused by coxsackievirus; herpangina is limited to the mouth.

stem: Fill in the blank: a healthy newborn's social smile typically emerges by around ____ of age.
Fill in the blank: excessive, unexplained crying in an otherwise healthy infant, typically peaking around 6 weeks of age, is commonly referred to as ____.
Fill in the blank: jaundice appearing in a newborn within the first 24 hours of life is considered ____ and warrants urgent evaluation, unlike the common physiologic jaundice appearing after day 2.
Fill in the blank: extremely high unconjugated bilirubin levels in a newborn can cross the blood-brain barrier and cause a form of brain damage called ____.
Fill in the blank: the onset of secondary sexual characteristics before age 8 in girls or age 9 in boys is called ____ puberty.
Fill in the blank: a child's growth measurements are typically plotted on standardized curves as a ____, comparing them to peers of the same age and sex.
Which fracture pattern in a young, non-ambulatory infant should raise strong suspicion for non-accidental trauma (child abuse)?
choices: Simple greenstick fracture from a fall
Simple linear skull fracture with a clear accidental history

stem: Fill in the blank: infants exclusively breastfed are typically recommended to receive supplemental ____ due to low levels in breast milk.
